title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' notes on tame ('modérée') topology. He is looking for a purely combinatorial axiomatics, called a 'magasin' (of multistructures), for the strata of possibly several stratifications of one space. The previous page is a crossed-out draft; this page is the clean version, and the next page passes to 'ateliers' (posets of figures).

Data: a set M with three relations ≤, ≪ and |∘|.
- Heuristically, elements of M are strata, each carrying the induced stratification of its closure.
- Y ≤ X: Y is one of the strata of the stratified closure of X. X̃ = {Y : Y ≤ X} is the set of strata of X̄ (the 'structure' of the figure X̄).
- Z ≪ X: Z lies in the closure of X as a set, possibly coming from another stratification. This is the 'shadow' relation, Omb, of the previous page.
- X |∘| Y: X and Y are 'stratifiquement disjoints', i.e. the open strata X°, Y° are disjoint.

Mag1: ≤ and ≪ are partial orders, and ≤ ⇒ ≪.

Mag2: if Z ≪ X, the set X̃^Z = {X' ∈ X̃ | Z ≪ X'} has a least element. This set is non-empty since it contains X. Geometrically, the least element is the stratum of X̄ containing the generic part of Z. When that least element is X itself, write Z ∘≪ X ('Z is generically in the open stratum X').

Mag3: |∘| is symmetric and irreflexive. It is stable under passing to things generically inside: X|∘|Y, X' ∘≪ X, Y' ∘≪ Y ⇒ X'|∘|Y'.

Mag4: distinct strata of one closure are disjoint: Y, Z ≤ X, Y ≠ Z ⇒ Y|∘|Z. Together with Mag1, Y < Z ≤ X forces Y|∘|Z. So ≤ is the frontier/specialisation order of a stratification, not set-inclusion.

Derived notions:
- X ≭ Y ('compatible'): all strata of X̄ not shared with Ȳ are disjoint from all strata of Ȳ not shared with X̄. In other words, the two induced stratifications glue to a stratification of X̄ ∪ Ȳ.
- X ∥ Y: every stratum of X̃ is disjoint from every stratum of Ỹ, i.e. the closures are disjoint.
- Claim: X ∥ Y ⇔ X ≭ Y and X̃ ∩ Ỹ = ∅, i.e. {X,Y} has no lower bound in (M,≤).
  - Proof (⇒): a common W would give W|∘|W, contradicting irreflexivity.
  - Proof (⇐): if X̃ ∩ Ỹ = ∅, the definition of ≭ reduces to that of ∥.

Figure of a magasin: a ≤-downward-closed subset F whose elements are pairwise compatible (≭). Example: each X̃. This holds because, by Mag4, the elements of Ỹ∖Z̃ and Z̃∖Ỹ are distinct elements of X̃ and hence disjoint.

Purpose: build combinatorial models of tamely stratified spaces with several coexisting stratifications. Figures are downward-closed, pairwise-compatible sets of strata. The next page axiomatises the poset of figures ('atelier': closed under sups of bounded families, every figure the sup of its strictly irreducible elements, which recover M).
errors: No genuine error. The equivalence X∥Y ⇔ (X≭Y and X̃∩Ỹ=∅) is correct and nearly tautological; it uses irreflexivity of |∘| (Mag3).

Mag2 as stated quantifies only over X' ∈ X̃. It does not exclude two incomparable minimal-looking candidates beyond requiring a least element, so the axiom carries real geometric content (irreducibility/connectedness of Z) that is not discussed.
Mag1+Mag4 imply that Y<X entails Y|∘|X, so ≤ cannot be read as inclusion. This is consistent with the intended meaning but is a point a reader can easily misread.

ideas.what: Axiomatics 'magasin': a set of strata with a frontier order ≤, a closure/shadow order ≪ and a disjointness relation |∘| (axioms Mag1–Mag4).
ideas.modern_name: Poset of strata of a stratification / abstract stratified set; face posets of regular cell complexes; combinatorial models in o-minimal (tame) topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (abstract stratified sets); Björner and others (face posets); van den Dries (o-minimal tame topology)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 announces tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures, but not these axioms.

ideas.what: Relation Z ∘≪ X: the least element of X̃^Z is X, i.e. Z lies generically in the open stratum X.
ideas.modern_name: Generic-point / specialization of strata (cf. constructible sets, frontier condition)

ideas.what: Compatibility X≭Y (non-shared strata pairwise disjoint) and separation X∥Y, with ∥ ⇔ ≭ plus no common lower bound.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogous to consistency/conflict in event structures (Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel 1981) and coherence spaces (Girard 1987)

ideas.what: Figures: ≤-downward-closed, pairwise compatible subsets. These are then axiomatised as an 'atelier', a bounded-complete poset generated by strictly irreducible elements.
ideas.modern_name: Configurations of an event structure / cliques; prime-algebraic, bounded-complete domains

missed.claim: The pair magasin/atelier is structurally an event-structure / prime-algebraic-domain duality, transplanted to stratified topology. Elements of M are 'events' (strata) with causality ≤ and a consistency relation; figures are downward-closed, pairwise-consistent sets, i.e. configurations. The atelier axioms (sups of bounded families, every element a sup of strictly irreducibles) are exactly bounded-completeness plus prime-algebraicity. Grothendieck arrived at this independently, from geometry, around 1986.
missed.quote: Figure F d'un magasin : partie ≤-fermée, telle que ∀X,Y∈F, on ait X≭Y. Ex : les X̃
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives a domain-theoretic (finitary, order-theoretic) model of the 'combinatorial skeleton' of tame stratified spaces. It could link exit-path / stratified-space combinatorics with Winskel-style representation theorems. That link does not appear in the literature on stratifications.

missed.claim: An axiomatic combinatorial theory of several coexisting stratifications ('multistructures') of one tame space, with gluing (compatibility) and separation, was begun here. It was never developed or published.
missed.quote: Un magasin (de multistructures) est la donnée d'un ensemble M, muni de trois relations ≤, ≪, |∘|
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Common refinements and compatibility of stratifications are central in o-minimal geometry and in stratified homotopy theory. A purely order-theoretic axiomatics of this kind is not standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a coherent, unpublished combinatorial axiomatics for compatible stratifications in tame topology, with a non-obvious resemblance to event structures and domains. The individual results on the page are elementary, however, and the program is sketchy.
transcription_corrections: '(i.e. {X, Y} un miroir des M)' should read '(i.e. {X,Y} non minoré dans M)'. This matches the condition X̃∩Ỹ=∅.
The relation symbol transcribed as '⊼' appears in the image as a struck-through ≍-type sign (≭), not as ⊼.
'En termes des Ẽn domaines, on définit' is probably 'En termes de ces données, on définit' (uncertain).
'Y ∤≠ Z' should read 'Y ≠ Z' (a stray mark was crossed out).
'On [conclu] a alors' is probably 'On a alors', with 'conclut'/'conçoit' crossed out.
